blogs.title: "Where Employees Lose Their Chance For Daily Wage Penalties"
blogs.description: "Following Consilio’s abrupt elimination of premium overtime pay, this post explores how Minnesota’s Payment Of Wages Act limits employees’ capacity to sue directly for daily‑average‑wage penalties—restricting remedies exclusively to agency action—and explains its implications for employers planning similar changes."

blogs.title: "Do You Still Stand Once You’re Paid Back"
blogs.description: "By unpacking Justice Kelly’s refusal to allow Cohen’s claim against statutory penalties after a settlement paid his overtime liabilities, readers learn why standing under Minnesota’s Fair Labor Standards Act hinges on ongoing harm—and how courts use Friends‑of‑Earth precedents to decide whether plaintiffs can press deceptive conduct once future recurrence becomes unlikely."

blogs.title: "Notice Is Key Life‑Sentence Under Minnesota’s Wage‑Theft Law"
blogs.description: "Despite an insurer objection concerning policy notices, the Court concluded the MWTA provides no avenue for civil penalties when employers miss forewarning requirements—illustrating the practical limits placed upon businesses attempting life‑long compliance through mere notification lapses."

blogs.title: "Settlements With Tailwind Claims Saggers’ Reclamation"
blogs.description: "Examining how Cohen’s parties agreed payments yet left selective claims alive pre-summary showcases why stipulating settlements does not extinguish pending disputes—even when paid overtimes are sworn—I discuss drafting tactics that preserve avenues such as injunctive relief post-seizure.”
